thread:
anna (cus-succ): Quick one — onboarding customer asking for an egress allowlist (IP ranges + ports + proxy requirements) so their security team can lock outbound rules. Can we give a concise recommended set?

mike (infra): Short answer: prefer FQDN allowlist (api.redwood.ai, models.redwood.ai, streams.redwood.ai). If they insist on IPs, give them our published prefix list + note it can change by region.

jess (security): Important: require TLS passthrough (no TLS MITM) on proxy for production. We rely on SNI and cert validation. If customer intercepts TLS, signatures break and streaming will fail.

sam (networking): Here’s the practical checklist I share with customers: 1) Allow outbound TCP 443 to api.redwood.ai and *.redwood.ai (recommended) OR allow the CIDR ranges below if they can’t do FQDN. 2) Allow outbound UDP/TCP 53 for DNS lookups (or point to a resolvable internal DNS that can resolve our FQDNs). 3) Proxy must support HTTP CONNECT and tunnelling for TLS and WebSockets. 4) Long-lived connections keepalive — don't aggressively kill idle TLS < 10m.

mike (infra): If they need IPs (per-region):
- us-east-1: 34.120.45.0/24, 34.120.46.0/24
- us-west-2: 52.35.200.0/24, 52.35.201.0/24
- eu-west-1: 18.194.120.0/24, 18.194.121.0/24
(These are example stable NAT egress ranges — for official list point them at our published url: https://status.redwood.ai/egress-prefixes — tell them to pull by region.)

jess (security): Ports: only TCP 443 is strictly required for API & streaming. Optional: TCP 80 to allow HTTP->HTTPS redirects during initial provisioning (not needed after). For health probes we use 443 as well. No additional custom ports required.

anna (cus-succ): Customer also asked about proxy authentication and TLS inspection — do we support upstream proxy auth?

sam (networking): We support customers sitting behind an authenticating forward proxy, but the proxy must allow CONNECT to our host:443 and must not terminate TLS. If they do proxy auth, the service account used for their infra should handle the session. TL;DR: proxy auth OK, TLS interception NOT OK.

mike (infra): Quick test snippet they can run from their network to validate egress:
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/ping --header 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>'
```
If they need to validate IP-level route:
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/ping --resolve api.redwood.ai:443:34.120.45.12
```
Replace IP with one of the published prefixes for the region.

jess (security): Also note: if the customer uses an egress allowlist by IP, they must plan for updates. We publish changes with 14 days notice for non-critical moves; critical rotations may be announced on status and via account team. Recommend they allow the entire prefix for the region to reduce churn.

anna (cus-succ): Perfect — can you boil this down to a 1-page checklist I can hand to the customer?

sam (networking): I'll drop a short checklist in the thread:
- Preferred: allow FQDNs: api.redwood.ai, streams.redwood.ai, models.redwood.ai (outbound TCP 443)
- If IP-only: allow regional CIDRs from https://status.redwood.ai/egress-prefixes (TCP 443)
- DNS: allow UDP/TCP 53 to your resolver or ensure internal DNS resolves our FQDNs
- Proxy: must support CONNECT, allow host:443, and MUST NOT perform TLS interception (no MITM)
- Keepalive: allow long-lived TLS (don’t close idle connections < 10m)
- Testing: use curl ping and --resolve to validate

redwood-deploy-bot: Notice: if customer is on Dedicated/Private with customer-controlled NAT, please open support ticket to coordinate IP assignment.

mike (infra): I'll convert this to the official one-pager and publish link in #docs when done. tagging @anna to follow up with customer. :thumbsup:

anna (cus-succ): Thanks all — will send to customer and loop back if they push for IP-only enforcement. :pray:
